name: multi_edit
description: Apply multiple find-and-replace operations to one wiki document atomically. Each edit operates on the result of the previous edit. If ANY edit fails (no match, multi-match without `replace_all`, or empty `old_string`), nothing is written and the whole batch is reported as failed. One commit covers all edits. Prefer this over multiple `edit_doc` calls when changing several parts of the same document — saves round-trips and gives all-or-nothing semantics. The file must have been seen via `search_wiki` earlier in the conversation, and must already exist (use `write_doc` for new files). Only call after the user has explicitly approved the change. Returns the commit SHA, the unified diff, and any broken markdown links the result introduces.

path.description: Wiki-relative path to the markdown file. Must end in `.md` and already exist.

edits.description: Edits applied sequentially against the running body. Plan them so earlier edits don't remove text that later edits look for.

old_string.description: Text to replace at this step. Must be unique within the running body unless `replace_all` is true.

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence at this step. Defaults to false.

commit_message.description: Short commit message summarizing the overall change.

base_sha.description: Optional. The sha you last read for `path`. When set, the batch aborts with `stale_base` if HEAD has moved since.
